html:
SMTO-CFG-0053 — SMTO's default Gateway name isn't in its list of Gateways

GUID: 6e465cbe-2dfc-443d-9fce-12536fac9f2a
Slug: config-default-node-must-be-one-of-the
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because its default Gateway — the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer — is set to a name that isn't in its list of Gateway names.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find where SMTO is started (the terminal command, a startup script or the service settings) and compare AOR_DEFAULT_NODE with the names listed in AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES. The default must be one of the listed names, written exactly the same way.
  2. Change AOR_DEFAULT_NODE to the listed name of the computer you want commands to run on, or delete AOR_DEFAULT_NODE if you don't need a default. SMTO matches names exactly, so a different spelling or capital letter counts as a missing Gateway.
  3. Start SMTO again from the same place where you changed the setting. SMTO reads these Gateway names only when it starts.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't set the default to a different computer just to clear the error; tasks without a chosen Gateway would then run on that computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected default_node (AOR_DEFAULT_NODE) because it is not among the normalized available_nodes built from AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES and gateway_endpoints keys.

What this means

  • A configured default_node is absent from normalized available_nodes. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A configured default_node is absent from normalized available_nodes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact default name with normalized configured endpoint names; this is not a connectivity result.

How to fix it

  • Set AOR_DEFAULT_NODE to an exact (trimmed, case-sensitive) name from AOR_AVAILABLE_NODES or a gateway_endpoints key, or unset it, and restart the Server. This is a name check only and does not test Gateway reachability. Settings.available_nodes currently appends default_node itself, so this check should not normally fire; if it does, report the build and how the settings were supplied.
  • Configure an existing enabled Gateway node and select it explicitly or as the intended default. Keep endpoint names and node identities consistent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended default resolves to a configured available node.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
